verdict.rationale: Aider is operated mainly through natural-language instructions. These can be typed in the chat, passed via `--message`, spoken with `/voice`, or written as `AI!`/`AI?` comments in watch mode. Aider can also infer which files to edit from the request alone. Community users confirm it acts on plain prompts. missing for 10: session management (adding files, undo, git, model switching) still relies on explicit slash commands rather than natural language.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
Your voice coding instructions will be transcribed, as if you had typed them into the aider chat session.
You can use aider without adding any files, and it will try to figure out which files need to be edited based on your requests.
AI! triggers aider to make changes to your code.
if you leave a comment like '# make this darker ai!', Aider will step in and apply the change.
